rationale: Evidence: iteration 5 changed only sensor_size (0.012 to 0.016) from the iteration 1 baseline and scored 59.03, below iteration 1's 75.97. Progress fell on the s-bend (0.29 to 0.163) and oval (0.16 to 0.154), while max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.063 and line losses did not clearly improve (slalom 1.9 vs 2.0). This meets the Evaluator's rule (1): progress is below iteration 1 levels with max_error near 0.06, so the larger footprint is costing signal on the bends. I therefore revert sensor_size to 0.012 and do not try further footprint changes. The controller (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2) and spacing (x = -0.02..0.02 at y = 0.04) are the iteration 1 values, so this candidate is the best raced design reproduced exactly. Its purpose is to check whether the 75.97 result holds. Iteration 1's s-bend progress (0.29) is well above every other run (0.15 to 0.16) despite similar settings, so it may be partly seed-dependent. Iteration 4 and 5 used the same controller with different spacing or footprint and both fell to about 0.16, which suggests the 0.29 may be a favourable outcome. The replicate tests that before I change anything else. Expected result: progress near 0.29 on the s-bend and 0.16 on the oval, score near 76. If progress again falls to about 0.16 on the s-bend, the iteration 1 result was luck and the next lever is kd 0.15 for the 0.23 s-bend oscillation. Hypotheses: (H1) iteration 1's progress is reproducible with this exact design; (H2) if it is not, the variation comes from seed or disturbance, not the design. Measurements wanted: progress and line_loss_events per track, especially the s-bend (to compare with 0.29 and 1.95), max_error and where it peaks, and steering_oscillation (0.23 at kd 0.2).
